messages.author: 84aac2580b195c68
messages.subject: function used for calculating factor loading matrix in "mirt" function
parts:
Hello everyone,


I need to know which function "mirt" using to get those loading matrix.

> mod1=mirt(LSAT7, 1)
Iteration: 126, Log-Lik: -194.548, Max-Change: 0.00007
> 
> summary(mod1)

Factor loadings metric: 
            F1      h2
Item.1  0.6796 0.46179
Item.2  0.0980 0.00961
Item.3  0.3774 0.14246
Item.4 -0.0415 0.00172
Item.5  0.7699 0.59276
freq    0.9982 0.99650

SS loadings:  2.205 

Factor covariance: 
   F1
F1  1


I went through the code but I think I am missing something.

Best,
Irshad

messages.subject: Re: function used for calculating factor loading matrix in "mirt" function
parts: itemtype type of items to be modeled, declared as a vector for each item or a single value which will be repeated globally. The NULL default assumes that the items follow a graded or 2PL structure, however they may be changed to the following: 'Rasch', '2PL', '3PL', '3PLu', '4PL', 'graded', 'grsm', 'gpcm', 'nominal', 'ideal', 'PC2PL', 'PC3PL', '2PLNRM', '3PLNRM', '3PLuNRM', and '4PLNRM', for the Rasch/partial credit, 2 parameter logistic, 3 parameter logistic (lower or upper asymptote upper), 4 parameter logistic, graded response model, rating scale graded response model, generalized partial credit model, nominal model, ideal-point model, 2-3PL partially compensatory model, and 2-4 parameter nested logistic models, respectively.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: function used for calculating factor loading matrix in "mirt" function
parts:
A good number of the functions in the package are written with S4 methods, therefore its generally better to check the source code for the full package (as I pointed to in your previous post). 

Also, ExtractLambdas doesn't rotate the axes, it just extracts the raw loadings from the S4 defined objects. See how the Exploratory-Methods work, specifically summary(), to understand what is going on. Cheers.

Phil
